title: Ensembles
summary: Un groupe d'apprenants imparfaits peut battre chacun de ses membres : vote, bagging, forêts aléatoires, ExtraTrees et boosting. Le workbook ajoute ce que le livre n'aborde pas : le gradient boosting (HistGradientBoosting, XGBoost, LightGBM), état de l'art actuel sur les données tabulaires. Tu codes le vote, le bagging, la forêt, AdaBoost et un gradient boosting minimal avec tes arbres du ch. 13, puis tu bats une baseline sur California.
objectives: Expliquer pourquoi un ensemble réduit l'erreur et quand il échoue (erreurs corrélées, biais commun)
Calculer à la main un vote pondéré, une itération d'AdaBoost et deux itérations de gradient boosting
Implémenter le vote, le bagging, la forêt aléatoire, ExtraTrees, AdaBoost et un gradient boosting de régression
Utiliser HistGradientBoosting, XGBoost et LightGBM avec early stopping sur des données tabulaires
Interpréter l'importance des features (impureté contre permutation)
Choisir entre bagging et boosting selon le biais et la variance du modèle de base

mylearn.purpose: Vote, bootstrap, bagging, forêt aléatoire, ExtraTrees, AdaBoost (SAMME) et gradient boosting de régression, construits sur tree.py (ch. 13) ; chaque membre est créé par clone() de model_selection.py (ch. 8) à partir d'un gabarit non entraîné.

api.signature: def plurality_vote(predictions: ArrayLike, weights: ArrayLike | None = None) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Weighted plurality vote: for each sample, the label with the largest total weight wins (weights may be negative, as in the book); ties -> smallest label.
api.oracle: scipy.stats.mode for unweighted votes + brute-force loop for weighted votes

api.signature: def bootstrap_indices(n_samples: int, n_draws: int | None = None, rng: np.random.Generator | None = None) -> np.ndarray
api.summary: Indices drawn uniformly with replacement (default n_draws = n_samples).
api.oracle: properties: range and shape, reproducible with the same generator, mean fraction of distinct indices close to 1 - (1 - 1/n)^n ≈ 0.632

api.signature: class BaggingClassifier(estimator: object | None = None, n_estimators: int = 10, max_samples: int | float = 1.0, bootstrap: bool = True, oob_score: bool = False, random_state: int | None = None)
api.summary: Bootstrap aggregating. estimator None -> DecisionTreeClassifier(); each member is clone(template) (from .model_selection import clone, ch. 8), its random_state drawn from the ensemble generator when it has one. predict_proba = mean of members' probabilities aligned on classes_; predict = argmax (soft vote, like scikit-learn; the book's hard vote is available through plurality_vote).

params.max_samples: int or fraction of n drawn per member

api.returns: fit -> self; predict -> (n,) labels; predict_proba -> (n, n_classes)
api.raises: ValueError if n_estimators < 1, max_samples invalid, or oob_score without bootstrap; RuntimeError if not fitted
api.oracle: sklearn.ensemble.BaggingClassifier(DecisionTreeClassifier()) — statistical comparison (random streams differ): test accuracy within 0.03, oob_score_ within 0.05; properties (number of members, reproducibility with random_state, distinct bootstrap sets)

api.signature: class RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators: int = 100, max_depth: int | None = None, min_samples_split: int = 2, min_samples_leaf: int = 1, max_features: int | float | str | None = "sqrt", bootstrap: bool = True, oob_score: bool = False, random_state: int | None = None)
api.summary: Bagging of DecisionTreeClassifier(max_features=...) with a new random feature subset at every node (feature bagging); soft vote; feature_importances_ = mean of the trees' importances.

params.max_features: features examined per node ('sqrt' by default, as scikit-learn)

api.returns: fit -> self; predict -> (n,) labels; predict_proba -> (n, n_classes)
api.raises: ValueError for invalid hyperparameters; RuntimeError if not fitted
api.oracle: sklearn.ensemble.RandomForestClassifier — statistical comparison (accuracy within 0.03 on moons and Penguins, same ranking of the top feature importances)

api.signature: class ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators: int = 100, max_depth: int | None = None, min_samples_split: int = 2, min_samples_leaf: int = 1, max_features: int | float | str | None = "sqrt", bootstrap: bool = False, random_state: int | None = None)
api.summary: Extremely randomized trees: members use splitter='random' (random threshold per candidate feature) and, by default, the whole training set (no bootstrap), as scikit-learn.
api.returns: fit -> self; predict -> (n,) labels; predict_proba -> (n, n_classes)
api.raises: ValueError for invalid hyperparameters; RuntimeError if not fitted

api.signature: class AdaBoostClassifier(estimator: object | None = None, n_estimators: int = 50, learning_rate: float = 1.0, random_state: int | None = None)
api.summary: Multi-class AdaBoost (SAMME) with sample weights. estimator None -> DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=1). alpha_m = learning_rate * (ln((1 - err)/err) + ln(K - 1)); misclassified weights multiplied by exp(alpha_m), then normalised; stops early when err = 0 (member kept with weight 1) or err >= 1 - 1/K (member discarded). decision_function(X) -> (n, K) weighted votes divided by the sum of weights (scikit-learn returns a 1D score in the binary case); predict; staged_predict(X) -> Iterator[np.ndarray].
api.returns: fit -> self; predict -> (n,) labels; decision_function -> (n, K)
api.raises: ValueError if n_estimators < 1, learning_rate <= 0 or the estimator ignores sample_weight; RuntimeError if not fitted
api.oracle: sklearn.ensemble.AdaBoostClassifier(estimator=DecisionTreeClassifier(max_depth=1), same n_estimators and learning_rate): estimator_weights_ and estimator_errors_ allclose, identical predictions and staged predictions on tie-free continuous data

api.signature: class GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators: int = 100, learning_rate: float = 0.1, max_depth: int = 3, min_samples_leaf: int = 1, subsample: float = 1.0, random_state: int | None = None)
api.summary: Gradient boosting for the squared error: init_ = mean(y); each stage fits a DecisionTreeRegressor to the residuals y - F(X) (on a random subsample if subsample < 1) and F += learning_rate * tree.predict. predict, staged_predict(X) -> Iterator[np.ndarray].

params.subsample: fraction drawn without replacement per stage (stochastic gradient boosting)

api.raises: ValueError if learning_rate <= 0, n_estimators < 1 or subsample not in (0, 1]; RuntimeError if not fitted
api.oracle: sklearn.ensemble.GradientBoostingRegressor(criterion='squared_error', same hyperparameters, subsample=1.0): predictions and train_score_ (MSE per stage) allclose on tie-free continuous data

notes: Composition : 🔨/📦 = 9. 📄 inclus avant le ch. 16 (Grinsztajn et coll. 2022) car il fonde l'affirmation « état de l'art sur le tabulaire » exigée par la bible §8. Gradient boosting from scratch : régression (loss quadratique) seulement, avec les DecisionTreeRegressor du ch. 13 ; vérifié sur scikit-learn 1.6.1 que train_score_ = MSE complète et que la boucle manuelle (moyenne initiale + arbres sur les résidus) reproduit exactement GradientBoostingRegressor(criterion='squared_error'). La classification par gradient boosting passe par HistGradientBoosting/XGBoost/LightGBM (📦). AdaBoost : SAMME multi-classe (vérifié : α = ln((1−ε)/ε) + ln(K−1), algorithm déprécié en 1.6), ce qui contredit l'affirmation du livre sur le binaire. Vote : Bagging/Forest prédisent par vote souple comme scikit-learn ; le vote dur du livre est plurality_vote, comparé en 🔬. Membres créés avec mylearn.model_selection.clone (ch. 8, exercice 8.22 : type(est)(**hyperparamètres)), d'où la convention stricte « __init__ ne fait que stocker » dans tree.py. Oracles statistiques pour bagging/forêt/ExtraTrees (flux aléatoires différents) ; exacts pour AdaBoost et le gradient boosting sur données continues sans égalités. 🏆 14.28 : RMSE ≤ 0,45 sur le test (train_test_split 20 %, random_state=42) ; vérifié : HistGradientBoosting par défaut 0,462, réglé 0,444 en 1,4 s ; forêt 0,505 ; ridge 0,746. CatBoost cité par la bible mais absent de l'environnement figé : mention seulement. Rappels : 13 (N−1), 11 (N−3), 7 (N−7) ; le bootstrap (ch. 2) n'est pas pris comme rappel car tout le chapitre le réemploie.
